The post The Largest Hyperliquid Treasury Is One Bad Day From the Red appeared first on BeInCrypto.
item.content:encoded:
Crypto treasury companies have had a brutal year, and most now sit on deep paper losses. Hyperliquid Strategies, the largest Hyperliquid treasury, was one of the few still showing a substantial profit on its pile of tokens.

That profit has now shrunk to a few cents per token. Hyperliquid (HYPE), the token the company holds, fell about 28% over the past month. 

A Profit Measured in Cents

The HYPE price stood at $56.94 at press time, according to BeInCrypto Markets data. Hyperliquid Strategies holds about 38.9 million HYPE, according to its latest results. As of October 28, its blended cost stood at $56.35 per token.

Follow us on X to get the latest news as it happens

That blended figure includes staking rewards. For the tokens it actually bought, the company paid $61.13 on average. That means those purchases are already underwater. 

The Cost of Buying Near the Top

The thin margin comes from when the company bought. During the September quarter, it spent $785 million on 9.1 million HYPE, its earnings release shows. That works out to roughly $86 per token.

BeInCrypto tracked that buying spree while HYPE traded near its record high. Every expensive purchase lifted the company’s average cost, raising the price HYPE must hold. 

The next earnings report could also take a hit. The latest quarterly profit came mostly from paper gains on HYPE, valued at a far higher price. If prices stay here, the next report would likely show a large loss.

The Smaller Rival With Room to Spare

Hyperion DeFi, a smaller Hyperliquid treasury, tells a calmer story. Its filing puts its average cost at $40 per token as of September 30.

Hyperliquid Strategies has almost no such cushion. A further drop of about 1% would push its blended holdings below cost.

item.title: AMD Stock Crashes Another 13% – What’s Driving This Crisis?
item.dc:creator: Luis Blanco
item.description:
Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) shares tumbled nearly 13% on Friday, November 20. The chipmaker has now lost more than 24% over five trading days. Three main factors explain the latest selloff, from AI valuation fears to new legal pressure. The 3 Factors Behind AMD’s Crash A stock selloff is a rapid decline in share prices

The post AMD Stock Crashes Another 13% – What’s Driving This Crisis? appeared first on BeInCrypto.
item.content:encoded:
Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) shares tumbled nearly 13% on Friday, November 20. The chipmaker has now lost more than 24% over five trading days.

Three main factors explain the latest selloff, from AI valuation fears to new legal pressure.

The 3 Factors Behind AMD’s Crash

A stock selloff is a rapid decline in share prices as investors rush to sell. In AMD’s case, several forces hit the stock at once.

1. Anthropic’s Rocky Debut

Anthropic’s rocky market debut weighed heavily on AI stocks. The company, which trades under the ticker ANT, slumped about 12% on its second day of trading.

That weak performance spread pessimism across the AI supply chain. NVIDIA fell about 7%, while Micron dropped roughly 12%. As a result, investors reassessed valuations tied to AI demand.

2. Mounting Legal Pressure

Meanwhile, several law firms announced investigations into potential securities class-action claims against AMD. The probes focus on whether the company misled investors about its ties with Chinese manufacturer IEIT Systems.

The investigations followed a report released the previous day. Consequently, risk-averse investors chose to reduce their exposure.

3. A Global Chip Selloff

A global semiconductor rout added further pressure. Overnight, chip stocks in Taiwan and South Korea led steep declines across Asian markets.

That weakness spilled into US trading, and the Nasdaq Composite fell nearly 3%. Moreover, AMD broke below its 200-day moving average near $429, which accelerated institutional selling.

What Comes Next for AMD Stock?

The short-term outlook remains uncertain. AMD is still a key player in high-performance computing and AI accelerators, and its long-term story has not changed.

However, AI valuation concerns, legal uncertainty, and a technical breakdown now weigh on the stock together.

Reclaiming the $429 level would mark a first step toward stabilization.

Anthropic’s trading in the coming sessions will also matter, since it now serves as a gauge for AI sentiment. If its shares stabilize, pressure on chipmakers like AMD could ease.

On the legal front, the firms have only announced investigations into potential claims so far. Still, a five-day loss of more than 24% shows how quickly sentiment can turn in the AI trade.

For now, investors will watch upcoming guidance and any updates on the legal investigations.

The post AMD Stock Crashes Another 13% – What’s Driving This Crisis? appeared first on BeInCrypto.

item.title: How Low Will Bitcoin Price Drop? Analysts Predict
item.dc:creator: Lockridge Okoth
item.description:
Bitcoin broke $60,000. See how low analysts at Wintermute, Cowen, and Rekt Capital think BTC could fall next.

The post How Low Will Bitcoin Price Drop? Analysts Predict appeared first on BeInCrypto.
item.content:encoded:
How low can Bitcoin go? BTC price fell below $57,000 on Friday, losing 30% in a month. Analysts suggest the pain might not be over. Most point to a bottom around $50,000 to $54,000. 

Bitcoin’s realized price sits just under $54,000. It is the average buying price of all Bitcoin holders. 

US spot Bitcoin funds have already shed about $3.47 billion this month.

Wintermute Expects Bitcoin Around $50,000

Crypto market maker Wintermute called the bear market unfinished in its November 16 update.

The firm pointed to the 200-week moving average near $68,000. That is Bitcoin’s average weekly closing price over roughly four years. Traders treat it as a long-term floor, and Bitcoin closed below it.

Money flows are the bigger worry. US spot Bitcoin ETFs are about $1.9 billion net negative in 2026. In 2025, they drew $21 billion in inflows.

“With flows negative and the 200-week lost, we expect pressure into the $50s, with Saturday’s $62k low the first level and the $60k put cluster on Deribit the next magnet,” Wintermute indicated.

A put cluster is a pile of options bets that pay out if the price falls to a set level. Both of Wintermute’s levels have now broken.

The Federal Reserve (Fed) adds pressure. Traders see a 97.9% chance of a rate hike on December 9. Higher rates hurt assets that pay no interest.

What Happens if Bitcoin Falls Below $54,000?

Crypto analyst Benjamin Cowen listed what Bitcoin usually does in bear markets. It typically falls in the fourth quarter of a US midterm election year. It also tends to fall after the first hike in a rate cycle.

Cowen said Bitcoin normally drops below its realized price, now under $54,000. He added that it then reaches the “balanced price,” which he described as “much lower” without giving a figure.

His on-chain risk gauge reads 0.167. In Cowen’s data, bottoms form when it falls below 0.1.

Meanwhile, BitMEX co-founder Arthur Hayes, now chief investment officer at Maelstrom, expected further downside, a remark he made when Bitcoin traded for $61,405 on Friday.

“Next stop … goblin town,” wrote Hayes.

Hayes gave no price target. “Goblin town” is trader slang for a deep bear-market low.

What Does Bitcoin’s Weekly Chart Show?

On the weekly chart, Bitcoin opened the week at $65,351 and fell as low as $57,100. That is a drop of over 10%, with more than two days before the weekly close.

  • The Relative Strength Index (RSI) reads 33.82. It means Bitcoin is nearing oversold levels, and selling may be stretched.

The RSI sits well below its own average of 53.89 and is still falling. Bitcoin’s weekly RSI last slipped under 30 in early 2026 and in mid-2022, near major lows. That leaves room for more selling before the gauge flashes oversold.

  • Volume profiles add another layer.

These horizontal bars show where traders have bought and sold most heavily in the past. Green bars mark bullish volume, while red bars mark bearish volume.

Between $60,000 and about $72,000, red bars outweigh green. That suggests sellers are clustered overhead, ready to meet any rebound.

Below the current Bitcoin price, the picture flips. Green bars outweigh red from roughly $58,000 down to $50,000, signaling buyers waiting lower.

That buyer zone overlaps the $50,000 to $54,000 range analysts flagged. It also matches the August 2024 lows, when Bitcoin briefly dipped near $50,000 before rebounding.

A weekly close below $50,000 would take price into thinner volume, where support is weaker.

Is a Bitcoin Bottom Closer Than It Looks?

Not every analyst sees months of pain. Rekt Capital says Bitcoin is less than 2% from forming a new bottom in the fourth quarter.

That would put Bitcoin back in step with its four-year cycle. The pattern describes Bitcoin’s habit of peaking and bottoming in roughly four-year swings.

Wintermute itself refuses to call a low. Still, it noted that weekly closes below the 200-week average have appealed to patient investors on a multi-quarter view. Earlier this month, Grayscale called the slide an attractive entry point.

Wintermute said it would turn less defensive only after:

  • A daily close above $68,000 with same-day ETF inflows.
  • A softer Fed outlook would also change its view.

The next tests come fast. The Fed’s preferred inflation gauge lands on November 25, followed by the rate decision on December 9.

Wintermute noted markets already price in three hikes by March. For now, Bitcoin is trading less like a hedge and more like a bet on US interest rates.

The post How Low Will Bitcoin Price Drop? Analysts Predict appeared first on BeInCrypto.

item.title: Nvidia and SanDisk Bets Joined Bitcoin in a $1.76 Billion Liquidation Wave
item.dc:creator: Kamina Bashir
item.description:
Some crypto traders lost money on chip stocks over the past day, without ever touching Wall Street. Their losses landed in the same pile as Bitcoin (BTC) liquidations. That pile hit $1.76 billion in 24 hours. Wall Street’s Chip Trade Now Lives on Crypto Exchanges A liquidation happens when an exchange shuts a borrowed bet

The post Nvidia and SanDisk Bets Joined Bitcoin in a $1.76 Billion Liquidation Wave appeared first on BeInCrypto.
item.content:encoded:
Some crypto traders lost money on chip stocks over the past day, without ever touching Wall Street.

Their losses landed in the same pile as Bitcoin (BTC) liquidations. That pile hit $1.76 billion in 24 hours.

Wall Street’s Chip Trade Now Lives on Crypto Exchanges

A liquidation happens when an exchange shuts a borrowed bet because the trader can no longer cover losses.

Crypto platforms now offer these bets on stocks through perpetual futures. The contracts track a share price, never expire, and trade around the clock.

SOXL, a fund that tracks semiconductor stocks with triple leverage, led the stock-linked losses. About $36 million in SOXL positions were liquidated, roughly double the XRP (XRP) total on Coinglass.

Bets on SanDisk stock and Nvidia stock followed, with close to $28 million liquidated in each.

Follow us on X to get the latest news as it happens

The Day Nvidia Lost Its Bronze Medal

The damage started on Wall Street. On Friday, Nvidia fell behind Alphabet to become the fourth most valuable US company. Alphabet was worth about $3.25 trillion. Nvidia sat at roughly $3.03 trillion according to Companies Market Cap.

The chipmaker had already slid into a bear market earlier this month. On Friday, its shares hit their lowest level since June 2025.

STS Digital CEO Maxime Seiler linked the crypto slide to the tech rout in comments to Forbes.

“This is a one-sided risk-off, with AI and tech leading it and Bitcoin down at $59,500.”

Bitcoin Loses $60,000 for the First Time Since July

The selling did not stop at $59,500. The Bitcoin price now stands at $58,558, down about 5% in a day. It is the coin’s first time since July below $60,000.

Some analysts had been watching that level. Katie Stockton of Fairlead Strategies told CNBC the bottom of Bitcoin’s trading range sat just below $60,000. 

That leaves leveraged traders with little room. If buyers fail to defend this zone, longs could face another round of forced selling. 

Stock perps now tie crypto leverage to Nasdaq trading hours. Until chip shares steady, their losses are likely to keep showing up in crypto liquidation totals.

item.dc:creator: Luis Blanco
item.description:
Robert Kiyosaki is once again welcoming a market crash. The “Rich Dad Poor Dad” author says he is most excited about Bitcoin’s slide and cannot wait to buy more. However, not everyone shares his optimism, as some analysts warn of a deeper correction ahead. Why Kiyosaki Welcomes the Market Crash The sell-off hit hard. Bitcoin

The post Robert Kiyosaki Cheers the Bitcoin, Gold, and Silver Crash. Here is Why appeared first on BeInCrypto.
item.content:encoded:
Robert Kiyosaki is once again welcoming a market crash. The “Rich Dad Poor Dad” author says he is most excited about Bitcoin’s slide and cannot wait to buy more.

However, not everyone shares his optimism, as some analysts warn of a deeper correction ahead.

Why Kiyosaki Welcomes the Market Crash

The sell-off hit hard. Bitcoin fell below $60,000 and now trades near $58,200. It lost 31% over the past month.

Meanwhile, gold and silver shed roughly $1 trillion in six hours after Fed minutes signaled further rate hikes.

Kiyosaki blamed problems at the Federal Reserve, banks, and bond markets, along with US federal debt near $40.6 trillion.

In contrast, Bitcoin’s hard cap of 21 million coins makes it unique money, he argued.

His stance is consistent. Kiyosaki has long targeted $250,000 Bitcoin and openly uses debt to buy assets. Not everyone shares that confidence, however.

Is the Crash Really a Buying Opportunity?

Some analysts agree. Ash Crypto listed six reasons why November could prove a strong entry point.

These include past cycle bottoms after US midterms and possibly completed pre-IPO selling. The analyst also cited rising bank holdings of Bitcoin ETFs, which already control about 1.24 million BTC.

Lower oil prices, improving US manufacturing, and typical post-midterm stock gains round out the list.

Still, caution remains. Veteran trader Peter Brandt noted that every major Bitcoin bull market has ended with a correction of at least 75%. Measured from the recent high, that move would imply roughly $31,500.

With Bitcoin down about 54%, that scenario would require a much deeper slide.

Other traders watch intermediate support near $55,000, now just 6% below current prices. Meanwhile, long-term holders like Michael Saylor keep emphasizing accumulation.

“I began buying Bitcoin at $20,000 a coin… after the last crash. Will wait for Bitcoin bottom again. Lesson: ‘Your profit is made when you buy…not when you sell’,” Kiyosaki said in another post.

Ultimately, the debate remains open. Kiyosaki sees a chance to buy scarce assets, while history leaves room for a deeper correction first.

The post Robert Kiyosaki Cheers the Bitcoin, Gold, and Silver Crash. Here is Why appeared first on BeInCrypto.

item.title: S&P 500 Drops Below 7,000 as Nvidia Faces Accounting Investigation
item.dc:creator: Lockridge Okoth
item.description:
The S&P 500 broke below 7,000 as Nvidia's SEC probe reportedly turned to accounting. See the next market triggers.

The post S&P 500 Drops Below 7,000 as Nvidia Faces Accounting Investigation appeared first on BeInCrypto.
item.content:encoded:
S&P 500 has dropped 3% on Friday, dropping below 7,000 to its lowest price in 6 months. This comes as reports suggest the SEC is investigating Nvidia’s accounting. 

Meanwhile, Nvidia shares fell 12% to $128 – its lowest price in over a year. NVDA reportedly accounts for 6.1% of the  S&P 500

SEC Probe Into Nvidia’s Accounting

The Wall Street Journal first reported the civil probe on Nov. 17. Its focus then was whether Nvidia’s disclosures misled investors.

Friday’s reports said the inquiry now explores potential accounting issues. The SEC has not confirmed the probe or named the items under review.

The executive running Nvidia has overseen its finances since 2013.

Colette Kress became interim CEO on Nov. 11 after Jensen Huang resigned. Nvidia’s filing said she would keep the CFO role.

One reporting change has drawn scrutiny. Nvidia stopped listing Singapore as a separate revenue region in late 2025, after it billed $10.2 billion there in one quarter.

Nvidia said it switched to grouping sales by customer headquarters.

The Next Market Triggers for Nvidia and the S&P 500

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent gave Nvidia’s board and outside counsel 10 days to answer questions. He asked whether Nvidia knowingly sold chips to China to lift earnings.

On Dec. 1, Huang faces closed-door interviews with three House committees. General counsel Tim Teter follows on Dec. 2.

Nvidia also held back its quarterly report, the 10-Q, after Tuesday’s earnings. The 40-day filing window from the Oct. 25 quarter end closes in early December.

Nvidia has settled with the SEC before. In 2022, it paid $5.5 million over undisclosed crypto mining sales.

Nvidia now trades about 46% below its 52-week high of $243.37. Its slide sits inside a wider AI and tech selloff that also hit AMD this week.

The post S&P 500 Drops Below 7,000 as Nvidia Faces Accounting Investigation appeared first on BeInCrypto.

item.title: Morgan Stanley Ends Anthropic Stock Support After Just One Day
item.dc:creator: Lockridge Okoth
item.description:
Morgan Stanley used Anthropic's full greenshoe after one day, as ANT stock slid back toward its $83 IPO price.

The post Morgan Stanley Ends Anthropic Stock Support After Just One Day appeared first on BeInCrypto.
item.content:encoded:
Anthropic’s stock is falling sharply, and Morgan Stanley, which was responsible for helping stabilize its price, has already ended a key support mechanism. It happened just one day after the biggest IPO in history.

Morgan Stanley had up to 30 days to use the mechanism. Instead, it closed the arrangement on Friday, as Anthropic shares approached their $83 IPO price.

The decision is good news for Anthropic’s fundraising, but raises fresh concerns for investors.

Why Did Morgan Stanley End Its Support So Early?

When Anthropic went public on Thursday, Morgan Stanley was responsible for helping stabilize its stock during early trading.

The bank had two options for covering 147 million additional shares sold to investors:

  • If Anthropic’s stock fell: Buy shares from the market, creating demand that could help slow the decline.
  • If the stock stayed above $83: Buy the additional shares directly from Anthropic at the original IPO price.

On Friday, Morgan Stanley chose the second option, purchasing all 147 million shares at $83 each.

This process is known as a greenshoe option. It closed the bank’s short position linked to those additional shares, removing a potential source of market buying support.

What Does This Mean for Anthropic Stock Investors?

For Anthropic, the decision brings another $12.2 billion in gross IPO proceeds, taking the offering’s total to approximately $93.5 billion.

For investors, the timing is concerning.

Anthropic shares opened at $111.50 on Thursday and briefly reached $115.10. They closed at $97.17 before falling as low as $83.93 in Friday’s premarket trading.

Anyone who bought near Thursday’s peak was already facing a roughly 27% loss.

Carsten Hesse, an analyst at Berenberg, told Reuters that investors were losing “an important potential source of buying support.”

The wider technology selloff is adding pressure.

The next major test is $83. If Anthropic falls below its IPO price, investors will face further losses without the potential buying support from Morgan Stanley’s now-closed arrangement.

That support was never guaranteed, and its removal does not mean another

item.title: Wall Street Had a Big Week. Why are AI and Tech Stocks Still Crashing?
item.dc:creator: Lockridge Okoth
item.description:
AI and tech stocks are crashing despite Anthropic's record IPO and Nvidia's beat. Here is what investors fear instead.

The post Wall Street Had a Big Week. Why are AI and Tech Stocks Still Crashing? appeared first on BeInCrypto.
item.content:encoded:
AI and tech stocks kept falling on Friday, despite Anthropic’s record IPO and Nvidia’s earnings beat. Anthropic alone shed nearly $200 billion in market value from its first trade to Thursday’s close.

Investors had hoped the pair would revive the AI trade, but neither did. So, what is happening to the tech stock market?

Wall Street’s Big Week Couldn’t Lift Tech Stocks

Anthropic opened at $111.50, 34% above its $83 offer price, before dropping.

The IPO itself pulled cash from other stocks. Funds sold other holdings to pay for Anthropic orders, then got far fewer shares than they sought.

Of about 1,200 institutions that placed orders, more than half got no shares. Cramer expected that cash to flow back into other stocks. Instead, the S&P 500 fell 2% on Thursday.

Nvidia’s revenue beat Wall Street’s forecast by $6.5 billion. However, more than 90% of its revenue came from AI chips and servers sold to cloud companies.

That ties chipmakers to a handful of big spenders. In November, 52% of fund managers polled by Bank of America expected a cloud spending cut within six months.

Microsoft and Amazon, two major AI spenders, slipped 1.65% and 1.84% on Friday. Chip and data center names such as AMD, Micron and CoreWeave fell more than 4%.

China added a fresh scare. Short seller Hunterbrook alleged AMD software reached a blacklisted Chinese server maker, which AMD denies.

AMD closed down 7.72% on Thursday.

Interest rates are squeezing all of tech, not only AI. Federal Reserve meeting minutes pointed to more hikes, and traders now treat a December rate hike as nearly certain, CME data shows.

So why are AI and tech stocks falling?

  • Doubts that AI spending will last. In November, 52% of fund managers polled by Bank of America expected a major cloud company to cut AI spending within six months.
  • Big investors are leaving tech. Fund managers cut tech holdings at the fastest monthly pace since 2006, the same survey showed.
  • The Anthropic IPO drained cash. Funds sold other stocks to pay for orders, and more than half of about 1,200 institutions got no shares.
  • A rate hike looks likely. Traders treat a December Federal Reserve rate hike as nearly certain.
  • China risk is back. A short seller targeted AMD’s China ties, and Nvidia’s forecast assumes no AI chip sales to China.

Is This Panic or the Start of Something Worse?

Dan Ives of Yorkville Ives & Co called the selloff panic, not a broken AI thesis.

“This is strong appetite for this major AI IPO in Anthropic, and it’s a big win for the tech sector after a white-knuckle time with Nvidia,” he said.

Joachim Klement, a strategist at UK investment bank Panmure Liberum, disagrees. His team turned fully defensive after the S&P 500 broke below its 200-day average, a long-term trend line.

The damage is already serious. AI cloud provider CoreWeave sits 76% below its record high and Oracle 68%.

What Could Turn AI and Tech Stocks Around?

Much of the selling may already be done. Hedge funds have sold much of their net AI stock purchases made since early 2025.

History offers bulls some hope too. The S&P 500’s last six-day losing streak, in April 2024, ended the next session. A record rally followed 26 days later.

This streak has left S&P 500 index fund holders 8.2% below October’s record.

The post Wall Street Had a Big Week. Why are AI and Tech Stocks Still Crashing? appeared first on BeInCrypto.

item.title: CoreWeave Briefly Trades Below $40 IPO Price Amid Financing Worries
item.dc:creator: Lockridge Okoth
item.description:
CoreWeave stock briefly fell below its $40 IPO price as a rising interest bill outweighed 168% revenue growth.

The post CoreWeave Briefly Trades Below $40 IPO Price Amid Financing Worries appeared first on BeInCrypto.
item.content:encoded:
Anyone who bought CoreWeave (CRWV) at its $40 IPO price was briefly underwater on Friday. The AI cloud company’s shares slipped to $39.96, as worries over its debt returned.

The drop came despite what the company called record third-quarter revenue. CoreWeave, which rents Nvidia chips to AI developers, grew sales 168%. Yet the stock has lost nearly 79% since peaking at $187 in June 2025.

Why Is CoreWeave Stock Back at Its IPO Price?

Shares fell almost 10% to an intra-day low of $39.96 on Friday morning, slightly below the $40 level set in CoreWeave’s March 2025 offering.

The pressure is coming from the balance sheet. CoreWeave borrows heavily to buy chips and build data centers. Its debt stood at roughly $47 billion at the end of September.

That debt is getting more expensive to carry. Net interest expense reached $846 million in the third quarter, roughly 23% of revenue. The company expects $1.05 billion to $1.15 billion in the fourth quarter.

Those costs drove a $709 million quarterly loss, up from $110 million a year earlier.

Co-founder Brian Venturo said this week he bought $30 million of CoreWeave’s bonds. However, the three co-founders have sold about $3.3 billion of stock since the IPO. Those sales overshadowed the bond purchase.

Can Demand Outrun CoreWeave’s Interest Bill?

The business itself keeps growing. CoreWeave’s backlog, meaning revenue already signed under contract, reached $132.5 billion at the end of September. It also lifted its 2026 sales forecast to between $13 billion and $13.3 billion.

On the Nov. 10 earnings call, CEO Michael Intrator ruled out unsecured debt at current yields. Unsecured debt is borrowing not backed by specific assets. Instead, the company expects about $9 billion in customer prepayments and deposits within three months.

The stock rallied nearly 25% the next day. Those gains have since vanished.

Truist reiterated a Buy rating and a $115 target on Nov. 19. DA Davidson cut its target to $45 from $100.

The selling also hit other neoclouds, the companies that rent out AI computing power. Nebius and IREN fell roughly 10% and 11% in Friday morning trading.

Meanwhile, investor Michael Burry said this week that he had warned about Nvidia, CoreWeave and Nebius. He is holding bearish options positions.

item.title: Bitcoin Drops Below $60,000 for First Time Since July
item.dc:creator: Lockridge Okoth
item.description:
Bitcoin fell below $60,000 for the first time since July, even as US inflation expectations dropped to 3.7%. Here's why.

The post Bitcoin Drops Below $60,000 for First Time Since July appeared first on BeInCrypto.
item.content:encoded:
Bitcoin (BTC) fell below $60,000 on Friday for the first time since July. It touched $59,850 on Binance less than an hour after Americans said they expect inflation to cool.

That should have been good news for risky assets. It was not. Traders still see a 97.9% chance the Federal Reserve (Fed) raises rates on December 9, CME FedWatch data shows.

What Did Americans Just Say About Inflation?

Americans now expect 3.7% inflation over the next year, down from 4.7% in October, a University of Michigan survey showed. Cheaper gas helped.

The news killed one bet. A week ago, traders gave a half-point “jumbo” hike 11.5% odds. By Friday morning, those odds hit zero.

But a smaller hike is still a hike. It would extend a run that began with the Fed’s first hike in three years in September.

Why Is Bitcoin Still Falling?

Higher rates hurt assets that pay nothing. They make gold costlier to hold. Bitcoin pays no interest either.

Big investors are also heading for the exits. US Bitcoin funds have lost about $3.47 billion this month, including BlackRock’s record $541 million outflow.

Bitcoin had already slipped to its estimated $62,000 mining cost on Thursday. Friday’s drop pushed it lower still.

Gold slid after the survey too, before paring losses.

Is the Fed Listening to Cheaper Gas?

Not yet. Most Fed officials feared inflation could stick even if gas prices kept falling, October meeting minutes showed.

Fed Governor Christopher Waller still wants a half-point hike.

“If you really want to get it down, you’ve got to start taking more aggressive actions,” AP reported.

Even Friday’s survey shows scars. Both inflation gauges remain above levels seen before the Iran war began in February.

The Fed’s preferred inflation gauge lands November 25. On December 9, Bitcoin holders learn whether the Fed shares Americans’ optimism.

The post Bitcoin Drops Below $60,000 for First Time Since July appeared first on BeInCrypto.

item.title: Why Are Cyber Attacks Increasing So Fast in 2026?
item.dc:creator: Jakub Dziadkowiec
item.description:
Cyber attacks go vertical in 2026 as AI tools arm hackers, with incidents doubling since August and crypto hit hardest.

The post Why Are Cyber Attacks Increasing So Fast in 2026? appeared first on BeInCrypto.
item.content:encoded:
Estimated cyber attacks have more than doubled in roughly three months, Bridgewater Associates data shows. The jump began when a Chinese AI model with strong hacking skills became free to download.

Bridgewater has not proven the model caused the spike. Still, the fund now prices in a one-in-three chance of an economically destabilizing cyber attack within a year. Banks, payment firms, and crypto exchanges sit closest to that risk.

Why Did Cyber Attacks Go Vertical After August?

Capriole Investments founder Charles Edwards shared the chart on X on Nov. 20. His verdict was three words long, “truly unprecedented times.”

For nearly a decade, Bridgewater’s annualized estimate climbed slowly. It rose from about 1,500 incidents in 2017 to roughly 4,000 by mid-2026, according to the research.

Then the line turned almost straight up, reaching nearly 10,000 by November. The chart marks a single event at the turning point.

That event is the late-August release of GLM 5.3’s weights. GLM 5.3 is a coding model from Beijing-based Z.ai, formerly Zhipu AI, and anyone can download and modify it.

The US National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) called it “the most cyber-capable open-weight model released to date” in its assessment.

Separately, the FBI warned on Nov. 13 that hackers have used ARTEX, an open-source AI hacking framework, since at least August. Some intrusions reached privileged access in under three hours, the bureau said. However, it found DeepSeek models, not GLM, most common in attacker setups.

How Fast Are Cyber Attacks Rising Month by Month?

Check Point Research data points the same way, though less steeply. The firm tracks average weekly attacks per organization worldwide.

Growth stayed modest in the first half and even dipped below 2025 levels in March. From July, however, the yearly gap widened each month before peaking in September.

October cooled 9% from September but still ran 32% above last year. Ransomware hit a record 1,063 attacks that month, according to Check Point.

n0n, one of October’s most active ransomware groups, claimed this week’s breach of vendors serving JPMorgan Chase, Visa, and Mastercard. Attackers accessed customer names and email addresses, Bloomberg reported.

Why Is Crypto Taking the Costliest Hits?

Crypto platforms absorb the largest losses. Binance lost about $6.3 billion on Oct. 29, the biggest crypto theft on record. The breach began with a fake job interview that planted malware on an engineer’s computer.

Before that single incident, DefiLlama had already logged 312 crypto hacks worth $2.4 billion in 2026. Meanwhile, Chainalysis estimates that suspected North Korean groups caused nearly 89% of this year’s hack losses. In 2021, their share was 15%.

Scams add to the toll. US victims reported $11.37 billion in crypto-related fraud losses in 2025, over half of all cybercrime losses tracked by the FBI.

Are Defenders Already Falling Behind?

Experts on BeInCrypto’s Market Intelligence Expert Council argue that AI currently favors attackers. Erica Stanford, a digital assets and AI adviser at law firm CMS and author of Crypto Wars, made that case in a recent discussion.

“It’s 100% helping criminals… anyone with no skills and not even native English or native language can now commit fraud and crimes very very easily because AI helps people do that.”

Patrick Prinz, co-founder of asset recovery firm Recoveris, agreed.

“I think it’s enabling criminals more than it helps right now the law enforcement side.”

Recovery also trails the theft itself. Binance has secured an Abu Dhabi court order over frozen funds, yet most stolen assets remain out of reach.

Prinz expects years to pass before law enforcement fields a matching response. Until then, every exchange, bank, and vendor faces attackers working at machine speed, and Bridgewater’s curve shows no sign of flattening.

item.content:encoded:
US spot XRP (XRP) ETFs have gone 15 straight trading days without an inflow, their longest drought since launch. Meanwhile, XRP supply on Binance has tightened past its July level.

Thin exchange supply can limit selling pressure. However, it only supports prices when buyers show up. That puts the spotlight on ETF investors, who have stayed away since late October.

October 29 Was the Last Day XRP ETFs Took In Money

The funds last drew a net inflow of $8.43 million on October 29, SoSoValue data shows. Since then, they have shed $26.29 million. The previous longest dry spell lasted 8 trading days, from March 5 to 16.

The outflows now span 3 straight weeks. The funds lost $6.14 million on November 17 alone. That followed $19.13 million in withdrawals during the week ending November 13, an 8-month weekly high.

Total net assets slid to $1.08 billion by November 19, down from $1.77 billion on September 25.

Still, cumulative net inflows since launch stand near $1.78 billion. Existing holders have largely stayed, while new money has paused.

On Binance, the picture looks different. CryptoQuant’s Supply Shortage Index tracks how scarce XRP is on the exchange.

The index reached 2.4 on November 19, above its July 6 reading of 2.09, analyst Amr Taha noted. Readings above 2 point to severe tightness.

XRP whales have been pulling coins off the exchange too. They withdrew over $127 million net between November 10 and 16, analyst Darkfost reported.

However, Darkfost added that part of that flow may be internal Binance transfers. He saw similar moves after the exchange’s $6.3 billion hack, when it rebuilt reserves.

Follow us on X to get the latest news as it happens

Can Tight Supply Lift the XRP Price Without ETF Buyers?

XRP price stood at $0.96581 at press time, according to BeInCrypto Markets data. The token has lost 3.61% over the past week.

Risk-adjusted returns also look weak. XRP’s 30-day Sharpe ratio sits near -0.41. A negative reading means its recent returns have fallen short of the risk its price swings carry.

XRP also trades below its 200-day moving average, which sits near $1.26. Taha said tighter supply could help a recovery if buyers return. On its own, though, it does not confirm a reversal.

Arab Chain pointed to improving Sharpe readings and a reclaim of key technical levels as the signals to watch.

A return of XRP ETF inflows would be the first sign that demand is meeting Binance’s thin supply.
